candidates.rationale: The gap between price and its EMA is accumulated one-sided order flow that liquidity providers must unwind; dividing by the name's own price dispersion makes a 2% stretch in a quiet stock count more than in a jumpy one, and the stretch closes over the next days.

A name sitting high in its 10-day range but low in its 63-day range has been bid up faster than its own recent norm; that excess overreaction mean-reverts, while the raw range position on its own is confounded with genuine trend.

Campbell-Grossman-Wang: a daily move on unusually heavy dollar volume is more likely uninformed liquidity demand bought with a price concession, so it reverses, whereas the same move on light volume is more likely information and persists.

Intraday open-to-close returns are where liquidity demanders pay the spread, so a run of intraday declines is accumulated selling pressure that gets repaid; the overnight leg carries news and does not reverse, so isolating the intraday leg cleans the reversal.

Reversal is payment for supplying liquidity and is largest where a move is least likely to be news; in high book-to-price names more of the price variation comes from sentiment and flow rather than cash-flow revisions, so their weekly moves snap back harder.

Two horizons with opposite signs: information diffuses slowly over months (continuation) while the last two weeks are dominated by inventory pressure (reversal), so netting them isolates intact trends that have just overshot.

Path efficiency: net drift divided by total path length separates a quarter's move delivered in a straight line (steady information diffusion, little disagreement) from the same move churned out of noise; smooth trends continue, jagged ones are round trips.

Anchoring on the running high caps what traders will bid when price nears its peak, so good news is impounded with a delay; the delay is longest in high-volatility names where fundamental value is hardest to pin down, which is where the drift is collected.

A run-up backed by accruals rather than cash earnings is extrapolative and reverses, while the same run-up in a low-accrual name is backed by realised cash and persists; as a pure interaction it is orthogonal to both momentum and accruals standalone.

Fundamental-price gap: profitability improved over the past quarter but the price has not followed, so the fundamental change is not yet impounded and closes over subsequent months; symmetrically, price run-ups with no profitability support give back the gain.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.
